newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends flat after c.bank buys dollars.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends flat after c.bank buys dollars.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,500-1,501 per dollar, in a narrower spread from the morning's 1,499-1,502, as the central bank was seen as the main foreign currency buyer on a dollar-bearish market, dealers said.

"The market was very dormant with sporadic deals around 1,500 levs per dollar. Foreign currency demand from commercial banks and end customers was low and it was dollar byuing by the central bank that prevented a lev rise," one dealer said.
Traders said the central bank purchased dollars at 1,500-1,501 levs.
Central bank officials were not available for comment.
The lev closed at 884-889 per mark, tracking the dollar/mark cross on international markets.

Banks and clients continued to offer relatively large foreign currency volumes to improve lev liquidity and invest in high-yielding lev-denominated government securities despite a cut in central bank main interest rate, dealers said.
The central bank main interest rate now is 5.2 percent monthly, down from 6.2 percent last week. It stood at 18 percent monthly at the beginning of March.
The Finance ministry today offered three floating interest T-bill issues with maturities of six-, nine- and 12 months with no minimum acceptable price set in advance.
Interest on the T-bills equals the main interest rate and is adjusted each time the rate changes.
